scope: Editorial reading help. Definitions introduce finite computational examples and do not replace each work's hypotheses or upgrade its evidence.

background.papers: Vectors, matrices, linear maps, kernels and images, and reading a statement with hypotheses. Consult the selected paper for any additional algebra or analysis it uses.
background.monographs: Begin with the introduction and glossary. Then use the volume's own definitions to identify the background needed for its subject.
background.research: Read the problem statement, recorded scope and open questions first. The program's definitions determine its subject prerequisites.
background.packages: Basic command-line use and the package's programming language. Check its platform requirements before installation.
background.experiments: Basic programming and familiarity with the stated data and evaluation method. Read the input limits and acceptance criteria before interpreting output.

glossary.definition: A way to represent a declared system using concrete spaces and operations. The finite matrix implementation assigns a vector-space dimension to each type and a matrix to each allowed arrow.
Initial generating data from which an operator action produces further elements.
A name for a legal operator path or a packet coordinate. Different domains use addresses such as residues, signal phases or tree paths.
An operator P satisfying P² = P. Applying it again preserves the component already selected. A component in a redundant representation need not be a projector.

In the finite projector setting, a component selected by one projector in a complete family. The family separates an object into components that can be put back together. Other domains give packet their own definitions.
Values that describe an object relative to a chosen representation. A coordinate change changes that description while preserving the object under the stated transformation rules.
Analysis sends an object to coordinates. Synthesis reconstructs the object from them. The finite system checks SA = I, where A analyzes and S synthesizes.
The part of an operation connecting one source component to one target component. In a projector system it has the form QⱼTPᵢ. The blocks reconstruct the full operator under the packet hypotheses.
A compatible move from a coarser description to a finer one. In finite packet refinement, each fine packet has a coarse parent and each coarse projector equals the sum of its children.
A recorded discrepancy used to check a stated identity or computation. Its acceptance rule depends on the operation. A small numerical residual does not by itself establish a general theorem.
A reason a requested construction cannot meet its conditions. A carrier-change obstruction can exhibit two inputs identified by one representation that another representation must distinguish.

A structured report containing validity, evidence class, residuals and assumptions. Its producer defines what was checked. A saved certificate describes a past calculation and needs revalidation for a new one.
Computed using exact finite algebra or arithmetic under the stated hypotheses. Exact describes the evidence class. It does not establish every supplied assumption.
Computed with floating-point arithmetic and interpreted using a stated error or residual rule. Even a zero observed residual does not turn a floating-point calculation into an exact-arithmetic proof.
A result that retains explicitly listed assumptions that the computation has not established. Passing its checks does not discharge those assumptions.

A recorded connection between a written claim and a formal Lean statement. Check the hypotheses, declaration, source edition and execution record. A similarly named declaration alone does not establish the connection.
